_comment: The single question bank behind institution-intake and the questionnaire. The HTML is GENERATED from this file (node intake/build-questionnaire.mjs); scripts/intake-check.mjs fails when they disagree. Every question carries the BrainKit home a SOURCED answer lands in. Add questions here, never in the HTML.

dispositions.SOURCED: An answer with a reference to a document, register or signed decision. Only these reach a BrainKit section.
dispositions.CLAIMED: An answer with no reference. Goes to the gap register with the respondent's role as owner.
dispositions.UNKNOWN: No answer. Goes to the gap register for escalation.

blocks.title: Regulated context
blocks.home: pointers only — the D6 data-risk register and obligations register

questions.prompt: Is there a brand guideline? Where does it live, who owns it, and when was it last approved?
questions.hint: The document is the answer. A colour someone remembers is a claim.

questions.prompt: Are colour, typography, logo and spacing available as tokens, or only as pictures in a PDF?
questions.hint: Tokens can be projected into the D7 brand seam directly; pictures have to be transcribed and re-approved.

questions.prompt: Are there tone-of-voice rules, or a list of words the institution never uses about itself?
questions.hint: Voice rules become the renderer's copy constraints.

questions.prompt: Which output media must look institutional: documents, decks, spreadsheets, web, wireframes?
questions.hint: Everything the harness renders for a human reads design.md.

questions.prompt: Is there a right-to-left or multi-language requirement?
questions.hint: The brand seam carries lang and dir; the renderer mirrors layout from them.

questions.prompt: Who signs off a new template today, and how long does it take?
questions.hint: This is a decision right; it also lands in block E.

questions.prompt: Is there a glossary, a data dictionary, or an adopted regulatory vocabulary? Where?
questions.hint: The binding vocabulary every artifact uses.

questions.prompt: Which words are contested internally (two departments, two meanings)?
questions.hint: A contested term stays a claim until one side's document wins.

questions.prompt: Which product and customer terms are legally defined and must never be paraphrased?
questions.hint: These are copied exactly, never reworded by the agent.

questions.prompt: Are there written architecture principles, or an architecture review board with a charter?
questions.hint: Principles every ADR must conform to.

questions.prompt: What are the binding constraints: data residency, integration patterns, hosting posture, identity provider?
questions.hint: Constraints, not preferences. Regulated constraints point at the D6 register rather than repeating it.

questions.prompt: What makes a change architecture-material here? What fires a review?
questions.hint: Becomes the architecture_material trigger in the institution profile.

questions.prompt: Which reference architectures or mandated patterns exist, and where are they?
The no-fly zone: which technologies must not be introduced, and what is the approved rationale for each?
questions.hint: Forbidden without a written reason is a claim, not a policy.

questions.prompt: The allowed set: the standard language, runtime, data platform and cloud, and the document that says so.
The consult set: which technologies need whose sign-off before use?
Which internal or external standards has the institution adopted?
questions.hint: By reference.

questions.prompt: Is there a curated package mirror or hardened-libraries supplier? Does the resolver fall back to the public index? Who owns the resolver configuration?
questions.hint: An unenforced registry is the honest answer if that is the case.

questions.prompt: The radar: what is being assessed, trialled, adopted or held, by whom, decided when, and re-decided when?
questions.hint: One line per technology: name, ring, owner role, since, review-by or exit-by.

questions.prompt: Who decides product scope, architecture, risk acceptance, data-protection questions, brand exceptions, technology exceptions, and release to production?
questions.hint: One decision per line with the accountable authority and who is consulted.

questions.prompt: Where are those decision rights written: a delegated-authorities matrix, committee terms of reference?
How does a decision escalate when authority is unclear?
Which humans hold the roles the Loom needs: product owner, engineering, risk second line, compliance, legal, operations, data protection, accountable executive, institutional-context owner?
questions.hint: Roles only here; names go in the identity registry. A role with no human is a gap.

questions.prompt: Who is the second human who merges what the facilitator proposes?
questions.hint: It is never the facilitator.

questions.prompt: What are the stated strategic intents for the current planning horizon, and where are they written?
questions.hint: Strategy paper, board pack, OKR set. Each intent gets a stable id (SI-01…).

questions.prompt: For each intent: the owner role and the measure the institution already tracks.
Which intents are explicitly not being pursued this cycle?
questions.hint: A problem that serves a parked intent should know it.

questions.prompt: Which regulators and regimes apply, in which jurisdictions?
questions.hint: Pointers only. The register holds the content.
questions.home: pointers only — the D6 data-risk register and obligations register

questions.prompt: Does a data-risk register exist? Who owns it? When was it last reconciled against the regulation?
questions.home: pointers only — the D6 data-risk register and obligations register

questions.prompt: Does an obligations register exist, with an owner per obligation?
questions.home: pointers only — the D6 data-risk register and obligations register

questions.prompt: Is there a jurisdiction profile per market, or one market only?
questions.home: pointers only — the D6 data-risk register and obligations register

questions.prompt: Who approves funding for change, at what thresholds? One stage or two?
What financial method is mandated: hurdle rate, horizon, NPV / IRR / payback, currency?
questions.hint: If none, say so. The business case then shows payback only.

questions.prompt: Which benefit categories does finance recognise, and which does it refuse?
How are benefits tracked after launch today, and by whom? Does anyone go back?
Which non-build costs does the institution routinely under-count: organisational change, training, legal and contractual work, control-function time, operations and run, decommissioning?
Is there an existing business-case template? Where?
questions.hint: If so, the Loom's template is filled from it, never the other way round.

questions.prompt: Where may institutional and personal data live? Is a collaboration workspace already approved for it?
Who would sign the residency record: data protection and risk second line, two different people, neither a builder?
questions.hint: Roles only.

questions.prompt: Which workspace tool would a Factory Floor project into, if any?
Who is the facilitator? Do they have Claude Code and the plugin today?
questions.hint: Role only.

questions.prompt: What is the institution's PII rule for interview notes and meeting notes?
questions.hint: If there is none, the floor's catalog-C banner is the rule until one is written, and that is a gap.
